headline: Leafs place Nick Blankenburg on injured reserve
take:
Daily Faceoff reports that Toronto has placed defensemen Nick Blankenburg and Marshall Rifai on injured reserve, which thins the Leafs' blue line at a shaky moment.

The numbers explain why it matters. Toronto sits at 6-4-2, but it has controlled only 47 percent of the expected goals (a measure of chance quality) so far this season, and at five-on-five that drops to 44 percent. The record has leaned on goals scored 4.7 above expected and goalies saving 4.4 more than expected, which can't be counted on to last. Neither defender has been a stabilizer. Blankenburg's five-on-five share is 47 percent in six games, though Toronto does a bit better with him on the ice. Rifai has played just two games, and the team's share has been 17 points worse with him out there. Both samples are tiny, so read them lightly. Losing them removes depth more than quality.

On the minutes, going by games already played without Rifai, Jake McCabe is up to 21:03 a night from 11:18, and Darren Raddysh is up to 24:17 from 22:34. Ekman-Larsson's new partner is Blankenburg's replacement. McCabe and Raddysh are the ones to watch.
